You extract source evidence for a paper-derived scientific benchmark. Return exactly one JSON object matching the supplied schema, with no Markdown or additional text.

Use only the fixed, line-numbered source packet. Do not use outside knowledge and do not infer an omitted coefficient, exponent, range, experimental condition, or uncertainty convention.

Extract at most one relation: the best source-supported executable quantitative relation connecting one to five numeric controls to one or two numeric readouts. A second source-reported condition is not required. Do not construct a pair, alternate world, counterfactual, task prompt, or benchmark design. If the source contains no complete relation, return {"relations":[]}.

The relation has exactly six fields: formula, parameters, controls, readouts, domain, and anchors. Formula.outputs is an executable expression tree for the source-reported central relation. Output keys must exactly match the readout names. A var leaf names a declared control and a param leaf names a declared parameter. Every declared control and parameter must occur in the formula. Numeric literals are allowed only for structural zero and one; encode every other scientific constant or fitted value as an anchored parameter. Preserve equality, approximation, fitted-relation, and asymptotic scope through the applicability statements; do not turn proportionality without its coefficient, an inequality, or an unspecified function into an exact point predictor.

A control is a numeric independent variable that can be queried within the source-supported domain. A readout is the quantitative dependent variable returned by the relation. Do not turn a latent quantity or an unreported fitted quantity into a control. Use continuous_interval only when the source supports a finite interval with minimum below maximum. Use numeric_values only for at least two explicitly supported numeric values. The domain must name every control exactly once. Record source-reported applicability or fixed context when present; otherwise use an empty applicability array.

Every formula, parameter value, control definition, readout definition, control domain, and applicability statement must carry direct inclusive source line ranges. Anchors contain line_start and line_end only. Do not generate a paraphrased support field. Use the line coordinates exactly as supplied.

Do not output source identity, schema version, an assessment, readiness flag, mechanisms, claim dependencies, ambiguity records, budget, diagnostic conditions, held-out conditions, public prose, provenance mappings, or code. Source identity and all benchmark-design fields are supplied or generated by deterministic code.

L003864	===== BEGIN FILE: body.tex =====
L003865	Flavor-changing neutral-current decays~\cite{FCNC2017}, such as the rare \decay{b}{s \ell^+ \ell^-} transition, serve as powerful and sensitive probes for physics beyond the Standard Model (SM). Their inherent suppression within the SM makes any observed deviation in their decay properties
L003866	a clear signature of new physics.
L003867	Since beginning of operations,  the \lhcb experiment has performed extensive studies of  a series of \decay{b}{s \ell^+\ell^-} processes, which have revealed a compelling, albeit evolving, picture of anomalies.Most notably,  the measurements of branching fractions and angular observables in several semileptonic $B$-meson decays performed by the \lhcb, ATLAS, CMS, Belle, and BaBar collaborations~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2021-022,LHCb-PAPER-2021-014,LHCb-PAPER-2018-029,LHCb-PAPER-2022-050,LHCb-PAPER-2014-049,LHCb-PAPER-2020-041,LHCb-PAPER-2017-001,LHCb-PAPER-2020-002,LHCb-PAPER-2025-041,ATLAS:2018gqc,CMS:2017rzx,Belle:2016fev,BaBar:2015wkg}  show a coherent and distinct pattern of tensions with the SM, which could be explained by new-physics contributions to the effective four-fermion \decay{b}{s \ell^+\ell^-} couplings~\cite{Alguero2023,Allanach:2023uxz,Capdevila:2023yhq}.
L003868	
L003869	
L003870	
L003871	
L003872	
L003873	These persistent anomalies motivate the use of complementary experimental probes to better understand the underlying dynamics.
L003874	 In particular, time-dependent
L003875	 analyses of neutral $B$-meson decays provide theoretically clean observables to explore new-physics phenomena in \decay{b}{s} transitions~\cite{Jager2013,Descotes_Genon_2021,Descotes-Genon2015,addref1,addref2,addref3,addref4,addref5,addref6,addref7}.
L003876	 The \CP asymmetry arising from the interference between  the
L003877	$\Bz$--$\Bzb$ mixing and decay amplitudes is sensitive to the imaginary parts of the Wilson coefficients governing these processes,
L003878	yielding constraints on new \CP-violating phases that are complementary to,
L003879	 and in many cases more direct and robust than, those obtained from the time-integrated or time-independent
L003880	 decay rates, angular distributions and  \CP asymmetries  in  decays such as $\Bd \to K^{*}(892)^0 \mup\mun$~\cite{Descotes-Genon2011,Fleischer:2025ucq,LHCb-PAPER-2024-011}.  The power of the time-dependent  approach is well established in hadronic \decay{b}{s q \bar{q}} $(q=d, s)$ channels, such as \decay{\Bz}{\eta' \KS} and \decay{\Bz}{\phi(1020) \KS}~\cite{PhysRevLett804625,GROSSMAN1997241}.\footnote{The inclusion of charge-conjugate processes is implied throughout this Letter unless otherwise stated.}
L003881	 The decay \decay{\Bd}{\KS \mup\mun} thus   enables  the first time-dependent \CP violation measurement in a \decay{b}{s \ell^+ \ell^-} process, opening a crucial new window to \CP-violating new physics in these rare modes.
L003882	
L003883	
L003884	In general, the $\KS\mup\mun$ final state is an admixture of \CP-even and odd eigenstates,  thus a full time-dependent angular analysis  is required to perform  the most complete test of \CP violation~\cite{Descotes_Genon_2021,Alguero:2021yus}.  Given the  limited statistics of the data sample considered in this Letter, this study
L003885	focuses on measuring the overall time-dependent \CP asymmetry after integrating over the lepton helicity angle in the dimuon rest frame.
L003886	The time-dependent  \CP asymmetry between the decay rates of  initial \Bzb and \Bz mesons to the $\KS\mup\mun$  final state is defined as
L003887	\begin{equation}
L003888	\label{eq1}
L003889	    \mathcal{A}^{\CP}(t) \equiv \frac{\Gamma(\decay{\Bzb(t)}{\KS\mup\mun}) - \Gamma(\decay{\Bz(t)}{\KS\mup\mun})}{\decay{\Gamma(\Bzb(t)}{\KS\mup\mun}) + \Gamma(\decay{\Bz(t)}{\KS\mup\mun})}\simeq S \sin(\Delta m_d t) - C \cos(\Delta m_d t),
L003890	\end{equation}
L003891	where $t$ is the time interval between the production and decay of the \Bzb or \Bz meson in its rest frame, $\Delta m_d$ is the $\Bz$--$\Bzb$ oscillation frequency, and $\Gamma$ is the decay rate for corresponding processes. The decay-width difference of the two $\Bz$ mass eigenstates, $\Delta\Gamma_d$ is assumed to be zero in the equation.
L003892	The parameters $S$ and $C$ quantify the mixing-induced and direct \CP violation, respectively.
L003893	 In the SM, the \decay{\Bd}{\KS\mup\mun} decay proceeds dominantly to a \CP-odd state
L003894	and  the expectation is
L003895	$C\approx 0$ and
L003896	$S =\sqrt{(1-C^2)} \sin(2\beta + \Delta\phi_d ) \approx \sin (2\beta)$. Here  $\beta$ is the CKM angle measured in \decay{\Bd}{\jpsi \KS} decays~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2023-013}, and $\Delta\phi_d$ is a small phase shift due to  the interference of the  \Bz mixing and \decay{b}{s} decay amplitudes.
L003897	For  the dimuon mass-squared range $1.1<q^2< 6.0$\gevgevcccc,
L003898	the mixing-induced \CP asymmetry  is explicitly predicted to be
L003899	 $S=0.72\pm 0.02$ in the SM~\cite{Fleischer2023}.
L003900	However, various new-physics models with new interactions or
L003901	additional weak phases can  lead to  a significant deviation of  $S$ and $C$ from their SM predictions~\cite{PRD107075}.
L003902	
L003903	
L003904	
L003905	This Letter reports the first measurement of the  \CP-violating parameters  in  \decay{\Bd}{\KS \mup\mun} decays using $pp$ collision data  collected with the \lhcb  detector in 2011--2012 (Run~1) and 2015--2018 (Run~2),
L003906	corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 9\invfb.
L003907	The \CP-violating observables $C$ and $S$ are measured from a time-dependent  analysis in the  full range of dimuon masses, $q^2$, excluding
L003908	 the $\jpsi$ ($8.0<q^2<11.0$\gevgevcccc)  and $\psi(2S)$  ($15.0<q^2<17.5$\gevgevcccc) regions.
L003909	The control channel  \decay{\Bd}{\jpsi(\to \mup\mun ) \KS} is used to  study the  difference between the simulation  and  data and to validate the fit procedure.

L003923	The \lhcb detector~\cite{LHCb-DP-2008-001,LHCb-DP-2014-002} is a single-arm forward spectrometer covering the pseudorapidity range $2 < \eta < 5$, designed for the study of particles containing $b$ or $c$ quarks. It employs a dipole magnet with periodically reversed polarity for momentum determination. The detector used to collect the
L003924	data analyzed in this paper includes a high-precision tracking system consisting of silicon-strip~\cite{LHCb-DP-2014-001,LHCb-DP-2017-001} and straw drift-tube~\cite{LHCb-DP-2017-001} detectors. Different types of charged hadrons are distinguished using information from two ring-imaging Cherenkov detectors~\cite{LHCb-DP-2013-003}.  Muons are identified by a
L003925	 system composed of alternating layers of iron and multiwire proportional chambers, achieving high efficiency and excellent momentum resolution~\cite{LHCb-DP-2012-002,LHCb-DP-2013-001}.
L003926	
L003927	
L003928	 The simulated samples used to study the decay properties of the signal, control, and background channels are
L003929	generated using the software described in Refs.~\cite{Sjostrand:2007gs,*Sjostrand:2006za,Lange:2001uf,Golonka:2005pn,Allison:2006ve, *Agostinelli:2002hh,LHCb-PROC-2011-006,LHCb-PROC-2010-056,LHCb-PUB-2016-021}.
L003930	        Simulated signal  decays are generated according to the theoretical calculation for \decay{b}{s} transitions in Ref.~\cite{Ball:2004rg}. The data-simulation difference is studied using the control channel \decay{\Bd}{\jpsi \KS}, and applied to the signal simulation to match the \Bz kinematic distributions and the particle identification (PID) performance in data.~\cite{LHCb-DP-2018-001,LHCb-DP-2013-001,LHCb-PUB-2016-021}.
L003931	
L003932	
L003933	
L003934	
L003935	The online event selection
L003936	is performed by a trigger~\cite{LHCb-DP-2012-004},
L003937	which consists of a hardware stage followed by a two-stage software trigger.  The hardware trigger  for this study
L003938	     employs information from the  muon system.
L003939	Subsequently, the  software trigger imposes requirements on the muon
L003940	transverse momentum and track reconstruction quality, or on the output of  a multibody  topological $b$-hadron trigger~\cite{LHCb-PROC-2015-018}.
L003941	Triggered data further undergo a centralized, offline processing step
L003942	 across the entire \lhcb physics program~\cite{Stripping}.
L003943	
L003944	
L003945	
L003946	In the offline analysis, $\KS$ candidates are reconstructed from two oppositely charged tracks  considered as pions. They are categorized according to the position of the $\KS$ decay vertex.
L003947	For $\KS$ mesons that decay inside the vertex locator (VELO), the resulting tracks are classified as long tracks and are reconstructed using hits from both the VELO and the main tracking stations, thereby providing the best momentum resolution. For particles that decay outside the VELO, the tracks are classified as downstream tracks; these are reconstructed using only hits from the tracking stations. The  mass of the $\pip\pim$ pair is required to be within $20\mevcc$ of the known $\KS$ mass~\cite{PDG2024}.
L003948	These \KS candidates are then combined with a pair of oppositely charged muons to form  \Bd candidates.
L003949	All tracks and vertices are required to have a good fit quality.
L003950	Furthermore, PID criteria are applied to ensure that the charged tracks are consistent with the hypothesis of being pions or muons, as required by the decay chain.
L003951	The PID observables of the charged tracks are calculated  using multivariate techniques to combine information from different subsystems~\cite{LHCb-DP-2013-001,LHCb-PUB-2016-021,LHCb-DP-2018-001}.
L003952	A kinematic fit is performed to improve the \Bd  mass resolution by constraining the mass of the $\pip\pim$  pair to the known  \KS mass\cite{PDG2024}.
L003953	
L003954	
L003955	
L003956	
L003957	This analysis considers specific backgrounds that can contaminate the \decay{\Bd}{\KS \mup\mun} signal sample. These include \decay{\Lb}{\Lz (\to p\pim)\mup\mun} decays where the proton is misidentified as a pion, and \decay{\Bd}{\Dm (\to \KS\pim)\pip} and \decay{\Bd}{\KS \pip\pim}  decays where two pions are misidentified as muons. These backgrounds are highly suppressed  through mass vetos and PID requirements. Evaluation using simulation samples confirms that their residual contamination to the final signal sample is negligible after these requirements.
L003958	The $q^2$ value is required to be outside the two defined charmonium regions, except when selecting the control channel  \decay{\Bd}{\jpsi(\to \mup\mun ) \KS}.
L003959	
L003960	
L003961	
L003962	To further suppress the combinatorial background arising from the random combination of unrelated tracks, a multivariate analysis based on a gradient boosted decision tree (BDTG) technique is carried out~\cite{Friedman2001GreedyFA}. The BDTG classifier is trained using simulated \decay{\Bd}{ \KS \mup \mun} signal decays  and  data candidates in the high \KS\mup\mun  mass sideband of
L003963	[5700, 6000]\mevcc  to represent the background.
L003964	The BDTG classifier incorporates a set of kinematic and topological variables, such as the transverse momentum (\pt) and $\eta$ of the \Bd and \KS candidates, their impact parameters  with respect to the primary vertex (PV), and PID variables of the final state particles. These inputs show good agreement between the background-subtracted data and simulation in both the signal and control channel \decay{\Bd}{\jpsi \KS}.
L003965	The  requirement on the BDTG output is chosen to maximize the expected signal significance.
L003966	
L003967	
L003968	Eight categories of  \decay{\Bz}{\KS\mup\mun} candidates are selected using separate BDTG classifiers, corresponding to the combinations of  four data-taking periods with roughly equal signal yields (2011--2012, 2015--2016, 2017, 2018) and two \KS categories (with
L003969	long or downstream track types). An unbinned extended maximum-likelihood fit is performed to the \Bd mass distribution  to determine the signal and background yields in  each category. The \Bd signal is modeled by a Crystal Ball function~\cite{Skwarnicki:1986xj}, with tail parameters fixed from simulation and the width and peak position allowed to vary in the fit.
L003970	The combinatorial background
L003971	is modeled with an exponential function.
L003972	
L003973	The mass distribution of the selected \Bd candidates combining all categories is shown in Fig.~\ref{fig1}, together with the combined fit results.
L003974	The total signal yield is  $941 \pm 55$.
L003975	All selected candidates are then sorted into two groups corresponding to the Run~1 and Run~2 periods, respectively, which are used in the subsequent decay-time fit to determine the \CP violation parameters.

L003988	
L003989	The decay-time distribution  of  \Bd (\Bdb) mesons produced in  $pp$ collisions is described by
L003990	\begin{equation}
L003991	\label{eq2}
L003992	P_{\Bd(\Bzb)}(t) \propto     e^{-t /\tau_{\Bd} } \left[\cosh{\left(\frac{\Delta\Gamma_d t}{2}\right)} \mp S \sin(\Delta m_d t) \pm C \cos(\Delta m_d t) +D\sinh{\left(\frac{\Delta\Gamma_d t}{2}\right)} \right]\,,
L003993	\end{equation}
L003994	where $\tau_{\Bd}$ is the lifetime of the \Bd meson. The  upper (lower) sign  corresponds to  \Bz (\Bzb) decays.
L003995	The parameter $D$  parametrizes \CP-violating effects originating from  $\Delta\Gamma_d$.
L003996	Since $\Delta\Gamma_d$ is  compatible with zero~\cite{PDG2024}, the $\cosh{\frac{\Delta\Gamma_d t}{2}}$ term  is approximated to 1, and the $\sinh{\frac{\Delta\Gamma_d t}{2}}$ term in Eq.~\ref{eq2} is neglected in the baseline measurement.
L003997	The reconstructed  decay-time distribution is affected by the experimental effects discussed below.
L003998	
L003999	
L004000	The  flavor of the $\Bd$  or $\Bdb$ meson at production is identified using both the same-side (SS)~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2016-039} and opposite-side (OS)~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2011-027} flavor tagging algorithms. The SS algorithm exploits charged particles from the signal $b$-quark fragmentation, such as pions and protons. The OS algorithm utilizes decay products from the associated partner $b$-hadron, including kaons, leptons, reconstructed charm hadrons, and the charge information from its decay vertex. Each algorithm provides a tagging decision $d$ with an estimated mistag probability, where $d = +1,-1$, or $0$ if the meson is classified as \Bd, \Bdb or untagged, respectively.
L004001	The estimated mistag probability is calibrated with a dedicated  software package~\cite{lhcb_ftcalib:2024},
L004002	using  \decay{\Bu}{\jpsi \Kp}
L004003	and \decay{\Bz}{\jpsi \Kstar(892)^0} decays  for the OS  and SS tagging method,  respectively.
L004004	The calibration samples are weighted to match the distributions in the signal sample of kinematic properties (\pt, $\eta$, and azimuthal angle of the signal \Bd candidates) and event characteristics (PV and track multiplicities). The package yields the calibrated mistag probability $\omega$ for each candidate.
L004005	The OS and SS tagging decisions and mistag probabilities are then combined to give the final tagging decision and mistag probability for each $B$ meson.
L004006	    The total effective tagging efficiency is$\etag$ $\left<D^2\right>  =(2.7\pm1.1)\%$ and $(4.1\pm0.6)\%$ for the Run~1 and Run~2 samples, respectively. Here \etag is the fraction of of $B$ candidates that have a nonzero tagging decision, and $D^2$ is  the effective dilution squared depending on the event-by-event mistag probability~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2011-027, LHCb-PAPER-2016-039}.
L004007	
L004008	
L004009	Assuming no production or tagging asymmetries for
L004010	\Bd  and \Bdb mesons, the decay-time distribution becomes
L004011	\begin{align}
L004012	\label{eq3}
L004013	P(t, d, \omega) \propto  \left[1 + d(1 - 2\omega\right)] P_{\Bd}(t) + \left[1 - d(1 - 2\omega\right)] P_{\Bdb}(t)\,.
L004014	\end{align}
L004015	The decay-time resolution is accounted for by convolving Eq.~\ref{eq3} with a resolution function
L004016	consisting of the sum of three Gaussian functions. Each Gaussian has the same mean and a width depending linearly on  the per-candidate decay-time uncertainty.
L004017	    The parameters of the resolution model are obtained by fitting the samples  of  prompt $\KS\mup\mun$ candidates,  which are constructed from a $K_{S}^{0}$ and two muon candidates passing the same selection criteria as that for the signal channel, except the minimum requirement on the  $B$ meson decay time.
L004018	
L004019	The resulting resolution model, with an effective resolution of about 60\fs, affects the \CP-violating parameters by less than $0.1\%$, which is negligible compared to the statistical uncertainties.
L004020	
L004021	
L004022	
L004023	The reconstruction, trigger, and selection requirements result in a decay-time-dependent signal efficiency. This effect is accounted for by multiplying the decay-time distribution by an acceptance function parameterized by a cubic spline function~\cite{Karbach-2014qba} with six knots at 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 8.0\ps  and eight coefficients. One coefficient is fixed to unity for normalization, and the remaining coefficients are allowed to vary in the fit to data described below.
L004024	
L004025	
L004026	A weighted unbinned maximum-likelihood fit~\cite{Plan2012,Xie:2009rka} is  simultaneously performed  on the Run~1 and Run~2 data samples to the decay times of the
L004027	\decay{\Bd}{\KS \mup\mun} candidates to determine the \CP violation parameters $S$ and $C$.
L004028	In this fit, only the signal component is explicitly modeled while the background contributions are statistically subtracted via the signal weights calculated  with the \sPlot~\cite{Pivk:2004ty} method  using the \Bd mass as the discriminating variable. This method   assumes that the decay time and \Bd mass are uncorrelated in both the signal and individual background components. Potential correlations are treated as systematic uncertainties.
L004029	
L004030	
L004031	In the fit, the \Bd lifetime and the mass difference between the two  neutral \B   mass eigenstates  are constrained to their world-average values, \mbox{$\tau_{\Bz}= 1.517 \pm 0.004\ps$} and $\dmd = 0.507 \pm 0.002\invps$~\cite{PDG2024}.
L004032	This allows the time acceptance  parameters to be  determined entirely from the fit to the signal data. The decay-time resolution  and flavor-tagging calibration parameters are constrained to the fit results obtained in the corresponding calibration  channels.
L004033	
L004034	
L004035	
L004036	
L004037	
L004038	The background-subtracted decay-time distributions of the tagged \Bdb and \Bd signal candidates in the combined data sample are shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:decaytime}, together with the  baseline fit using Eq.~\ref{eq2}. L004039	The \CP violation parameters are determined from the time-dependent fits both for the entire kinematically  allowed $q^2$ range (excluding the $\jpsi$ and $\psi(2S)$ regions) and, to probe potential $q^2$ dependency, in the $q^2$ ranges below and above the \jpsi region.  The results are   summarized in Table~\ref{tab:cp_results}
L004040	 and Fig.~\ref{fig:2dscan1}.
L004041	The 68.3\%, 95.5\% and 99.7\% confidence regions under the physical constraint $C^2+S^2\le 1$ are further obtained  for the total $q^2$ region using the Feldman--Cousins
L004042	method~\cite{FCscan,BAKER1984437} and  shown in the End Matter.

L004085	Several  sources  of systematic uncertainties for the
L004086	\CP-violation observables are investigated and listed in Table~\ref{tab:syst_sum}.
L004087	A large ensemble of pseudoexperiments generated according to the baseline fit results is used to validate the fit procedure. The observed distributions of the parameters from these pseudoexperiments demonstrate that the statistical uncertainties are correctly treated. A bias in the $C$ and $S$  parameters is  observed, which is due to the limited data sample size.
L004088	The consistency of the tagging calibration
L004089	parameters between the calibration and signal channels
L004090	is tested  using simulated samples, and that between \Bd and \Bdb mesons is investigated  using the calibration channels \decay{\Bu}{\jpsi \Kp}
L004091	and \decay{\Bz}{\jpsi \Kstarz}. The observed differences represent the leading source of systematic uncertainties.
L004092	Systematic  uncertainties associated with the modeling of the signal and background contributions are evaluated by repeating the mass fit with alternative functions, namely the sum of a Student's t-distribution and a Gaussian function for the signal and a second-order polynomial for the combinatorial background.
L004093	Then, the weighted maximum-likelihood fit is performed, and the differences in the resulting parameters from those of the baseline fit are assigned as  systematic uncertainties.
L004094	The effect of neglecting a small correlation between the reconstructed \Bd mass  and decay time in the signal weight determination when applying the \sPlot method is studied by reevaluating the signal weights in bins of the decay time and performing the decay-time fit again.
L004095	The effects of a nonzero $\Bz$--$\Bzb$ production asymmetry and a nonzero $\Delta\Gamma_d$ are evaluated by varying their values within their  uncertainties~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2014-042,PDG2024} and performing  the fits again. The resulting largest  variations in \CP violation parameters are assigned as systematic uncertainties.
L004096	The systematic uncertainties associated with  the decay-time acceptance and resolution models are evaluated using splines with different knot numbers and positions and found to be negligible.
L004097	The total systematic uncertainties, evaluated as the  quadrature sums of the contributions discussed above,  are
L004098	significantly smaller than the statistical ones.

L004125	The robustness of the analysis  results is checked
L004126	 by splitting the data sample by \KS reconstruction categories, magnet polarities, and data-taking periods,
L004127	 by varying the \Bd  mass and decay-time ranges, and  by obtaining alternative determination of the  $S$ parameters from the time-integrated \CP asymmetry.
L004128	The results are all compatible with each other and with the baseline fit results. As a cross-check, the analysis procedure has also been applied to the control channel  \decay{\Bd}{\jpsi\KS }. The corresponding results are consistent with those reported in Ref.~\cite{LHCb-PAPER-2023-013}.

L004133	
L004134	In conclusion, this Letter reports a measurement of the time-dependent \CP asymmetry in  \mbox{$\Bd\rightarrow \KS \mu^{+}\mu^{-}$ }  decays using data collected by the \lhcb experiment during the Run~1 and Run~2 data-taking periods.
L004135	The \CP violation parameters in the  full $q^2$ range, excluding the dimuon resonant regions due to \jpsi and \psitwos states, are determined to be
L004136	\begin{align*}
L004137	C &= -0.13 \pm 0.32 \, (\text{stat}) \pm 0.04 \, (\text{syst})\,,\\
L004138	S &= +0.82 \pm 0.29 \, (\text{stat}) \pm 0.05 \, (\text{syst}) \,,
L004139	\end{align*}
L004140	 with a statistical correlation coefficient of 0.50.
L004141	  This is the first measurement of time-dependent \CP violation in \decay{b}{s \ell^+ \ell^-} transitions, and the results are consistent with  the SM prediction.
L004142	This study  demonstrates a new avenue to probe  physics beyond the SM  in  \decay{b}{s \ell^+ \ell^-} transitions, complementary to measurements of branching fractions, angular observables and lepton-flavor universality observables.

L004149	\section{Confidence regions  within the physical boundary}
L004150	
L004151	The results shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:2dscan1} are obtained without applying any physical constraint on the \CP violation parameters. Confidence intervals satisfying this requirement are   derived using a constrained likelihood-ratio test. Specifically, the maximum-likelihood estimation and the ordering of parameter points are performed within the restricted domain defined by this inequality. The results are presented in Fig.~\ref{fig:2dscan2}. Systematic uncertainties are excluded from this evaluation as their contribution is negligible compared to the statistical uncertainties.

L004353	\begin{abstract}
L004354	  \noindent
L004355	 A flavor-tagged time-dependent  analysis of  \mbox{$\Bd\to K_{\rm S}^{0}\mu^{+}\mu^{-}$ } decays is performed across the full dimuon mass range excluding the \jpsi and $\psi(2S)$ resonance regions. The analysis uses  proton-proton collision data
L004356	 collected by the \lhcb experiment in 2011--2018
L004357	 at center-of-mass energies of 7, 8 and 13\tev, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 9\invfb.
L004358	 The \CP violation  parameters  are determined to be
L004359	\begin{eqnarray}
L004360	 &C=-0.13 \pm 0.32  \pm 0.04 \,,\nonumber \\
L004361	 &S=+0.82\pm 0.29  \pm 0.05 \,,\nonumber
L004362	\end{eqnarray}
L004363	  where
L004364	 the first uncertainties
L004365	are statistical and the second are systematic.
L004366	 The results are consistent with
L004367	 the Standard Model prediction.
L004368	 This is the first experimental study of time-dependent  \CP violation in \mbox{$b\rightarrow s \ell^{+} \ell^{-}$}  processes.
L004369	
L004370	\end{abstract}
